skill.name: controlnet-pose
skill.description: Use RunComfy CLI routes for pose-conditioned image and video generation with Kling Motion Control, Wan Animate, and Z-Image ControlNet LoRA.

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are mostly Markdown formatting, documentation links, and example RunComfy CLI commands rather than executable Ruby backticks or hidden file access. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or host reconnaissance intent was found in SKILL.md. The remaining concern is that prompts and media URLs are processed by RunComfy cloud services.

remediation.suggestion: Keep a clear notice that prompts, reference media URLs, and control images are sent to RunComfy services for generation.
Continue to require verified package-manager installation and avoid any remote shell installer pattern in future revisions.
Keep token path and file-mode documentation, and never instruct agents to read, print, or copy the token file.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Media Processing Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The skill explains that the RunComfy CLI posts model requests to the Model API and uses user-provided reference or control URLs. This is expected for the service, but sensitive prompts or media links would leave the local environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md directly states that the CLI posts to the Model API and limits outbound endpoints to RunComfy domains. The finding is a privacy disclosure risk, not evidence of malicious exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Pose-conditioned media workflows require choosing the right model and inputs. This skill routes Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through RunComfy CLI guidance for pose-driven generation.
actual_capabilities: Selects Kling Motion Control Pro or Standard for video motion transfer.
Selects Wan 2-2 Animate for stylized video-to-video animation.
Selects Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA for pose-conditioned images.
Shows RunComfy CLI inputs for reference video, character image, prompts, and control images.
Explains when multi-condition ControlNet stacks require RunComfy ComfyUI workflows.
Lists CLI exit codes and RunComfy troubleshooting references.
limitations: Requires RunComfy CLI installation and authentication before execution.
Requires externally hosted reference, character, or control images.
Does not create OpenPose or DWPose skeletons inside the skill.
CLI routes cover single-condition workflows; complex stacks require ComfyUI.

use_cases.title: Transfer Video Motion
use_cases.description: Map a reference performance video onto a target character using Kling Motion Control routes.

use_cases.title: Lock Image Pose
use_cases.description: Generate an image that follows a supplied pose skeleton, depth map, or canny guide.

use_cases.title: Choose ControlNet Route
use_cases.description: Compare video, image, and multi-condition needs before selecting a RunComfy workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Pose Route
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner route selection for a single pose task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this pose reference to create media of my subject. Tell me which RunComfy route fits and what assets you need.

prompt_templates.title: Transfer Video Motion
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate motion-control setup for a target character.
prompt_templates.prompt: Transfer a reference video motion to my target character. Use the draft-friendly route first and list any missing inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Choices
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced selection across Kling, Wan Animate, and Z-Image ControlNet.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the available RunComfy pose routes for this project: [project details]. Recommend one route and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Condition Control
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning when pose, depth, and reference images are all required.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a workflow with pose, depth, and character reference. Identify what the CLI can do and what requires RunComfy ComfyUI.

output_examples.input: A user wants a target character to follow a dance reference video.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Kling Motion Control Pro, requests the reference video and character image URLs, and describes the expected video output.

output_examples.input: A user wants an image that follows an OpenPose skeleton.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA, requests a hosted control image, and describes a pose-locked image result.

output_examples.input: A user needs pose, depth, and a character reference in one workflow.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that CLI routes are single-condition and points the user to RunComfy ComfyUI workflows.

best_practices: Use clean, well-framed reference videos with one subject and no scene cuts.
Host only user-approved media URLs before sending them to RunComfy.
Use Pro routes for final video work and cheaper routes for drafts.
anti_patterns: Do not use video motion routes for still-image pose conditioning.
Do not send private media URLs without explicit user approval.
Do not expect the CLI route to build complex multi-condition ControlNet stacks.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps route pose-conditioned image and video requests to suitable RunComfy models and workflows.

faq.question: Which models does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Kling Motion Control, Wan 2-2 Animate, and Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA routes.

faq.question: Does it create OpenPose or DWPose control images?
faq.answer: No. You must create and host the control image before using the CLI route.

faq.question: Does it support multi-condition ControlNet stacks?
faq.answer: It explains when to use RunComfy ComfyUI workflows because the listed CLI routes are single-condition.

faq.question: What data leaves my environment?
faq.answer: Prompts and user-provided media URLs are sent to RunComfy services when the CLI runs a generation.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
